regime.label: Dealer short-gamma field deepens as spot 1017.9 breaks under the 1040 flip toward a churning 1000 shelf
evidence: -7,893 total net GEX (gamma x OI x 200) across the whole 960-1150 chain with no zero-crossing anywhere: cumulative gamma is -12,545 below 1040 and only +4,653 from 1040 up, so dealers are structurally short gamma and hedging chases the move rather than fading it. 1040 is a per-strike sign change, not an aggregate long-gamma shelf.

-6,256 net GEX sits inside the 1000-1030 strikes alone, and spot 1017.9 now trades 22.1 points (2.1%) below both the 1040 sign change and the 1040 max pain, deepening the amplification pocket it entered yesterday at 1026.2.

+692 fresh call OI landed at 1020 and 1030 on 850 contracts of volume today, building an overwriting ceiling directly on top of spot, while the 1000 near put wall churned 374 lots for a net OI change of -6: the shelf at 1000 is being rolled, not reinforced, so its 1,857 OI overstates the support actually standing there.

6,281 contracts traded today, the heaviest in the visible 8-session window, with ATM IV up to 12.73% from 10.84% five sessions ago - volume and IV are both confirming the slide, which is the max-pain-failure signature, not a mean-reversion setup.

S50Z26.today_summary: 1017.9 on the Dec future, -8.7 points, now 22.1 points below the 1040 max pain that itself finally slipped from 1050 after six sessions parked there. Net GEX is -7,893 baht per point with no zero-crossing in the 960-1150 grid, so every hedge below 1040 sells into weakness instead of buying it. The 1,857-contract put shelf at 1000 traded 374 lots today for a net -6 OI change - rolled, not added - while +692 fresh calls were written at 1020/1030 on 850 lots, capping the bounce. 1-sigma is 8.16 points a day (0.80%), putting the 1000 strike only 2.2 sigma away.
what_changed: Max pain capitulated 1050 to 1040, the first drift in six sessions, confirming the option structure is following price rather than anchoring it.
Spot fell another 8.7 points to 1017.9, closing 8.3 points of the 26-point gap to the 1000 shelf flagged yesterday, and is now below the 1040 flip rather than approaching it.
Net GEX deepened to -7,893 from -6,445 yesterday as total OI grew to 29,564 contracts, so the short-gamma amplification got stronger, not weaker.
The 960 put wall added +340 OI on 649 lots to reach 2,686, but IV there softened 0.58 points and price is still 57.9 points (5.7%) away - a destination being stocked, not yet the live battleground.
S50Z26.five_day_thesis: 1066.0 five sessions ago versus 1017.9 today is -48.1 points (-4.51%), and over the same stretch call OI grew 32.2% and put OI 33.4% - OI building into a falling market is fresh risk transfer, not an unwind. ATM IV expanded 1.89 points from 10.84% to 12.73% and the 1-sigma day widened from 7.28 to 8.16 points, so the structure is pricing a bigger range even as the slide continues. The decisive migration is on the put side near money: 1000-strike put OI went 1,236 to 1,857 (+50.2%) and 960 went 1,963 to 2,686 (+36.8%), pulling the centre of parked downside risk down with price instead of defending the old 1050 pin. Max pain held 1050 for six sessions while spot walked 48 points away from it and only broke to 1040 today, which is the max-pain-failure pattern: real flow beat the option structure, so 1040 reads as a ceiling now, not a magnet. The 25d skew has sat between -0.18 and -1.94 all week and is -1.23 today, so this decline is still not being hedged with panic put buying - the IV bid is in near-money calls, which is what leaves the downside tail under-owned.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1000 / 960
strategies.rationale: Buys the cheapest vol on the curve (1000 put at 11.67% IV) and sells the richest wing (960 put at 14.07%) while dealer hedging below the 1040 flip sells into every down move, with the 2,686-contract 960 wall as the natural target 57.9 points lower.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid; max gain = 40-point width minus that debit.
strategies.invalidation: A reclaim of 1040 - the per-strike gamma sign change and max pain - puts spot back where hedging dampens rather than amplifies.

strategies.name: Call credit spread 1050 / 1070
strategies.rationale: Sells into the 1,635-contract near call wall at 1050 that is reinforced by the +692 contracts of fresh overwriting at 1020/1030, a supply stack spot would have to clear 32.1 points (3.9 sigma days) above here to threaten.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20-point width minus net credit received.
strategies.invalidation: A close above 1050 on expanding call volume, which would convert the wall into a short-gamma squeeze trigger toward the 2,314-contract 1100 wall.

strategies.name: Reverse iron condor 960/1000 put x 1050/1070 call
strategies.rationale: Pays for range expansion either way, which is the structural payoff of a -7,893 net GEX field with ATM IV still only 12.73% and rising 1.89 points in five sessions; the 1-sigma week is 18.2 points, so both inner strikes sit inside a single standard-deviation excursion.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = net debit paid, realised if spot finishes between 1000 and 1050.
strategies.invalidation: Spot holding the 1000-1050 box while ATM IV falls back under 11.5%, which would mean the short-gamma field is being absorbed rather than expressed.

S50Z26.prediction: Bias stays lower while 1017.9 trades under the 1040 flip, with 1000 the first contested level 17.9 points away - 2.2 times the 8.16-point 1-sigma day - and a break there opening 970/960 because short-gamma hedging adds supply on the way down and the 1000 shelf is being rolled rather than defended. 1-sigma to the 29 December expiry is 50.3 points, so the 960 wall is well inside reach without any shock. A sustained reclaim of 1040 invalidates this: it would put spot back above the per-strike sign change, with 1050 the next supply stack.
S50Z26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and none of these structures is a recommendation to execute. SET50 options are European and cash-settled on the SET50 index, so there is no physical delivery and no settlement-driven hedging demand: pinning to max pain or to a big strike is a tendency here, materially weaker than for physically-settled single stocks, and at 55 days to expiry it is weaker still. Defined risk is not low risk - the full debit or the full wing width minus credit can be lost, and the 960 wall is currently a stocked destination 5.7% away rather than a live battleground, so a 2,686-contract OI print should not be read as a guaranteed floor.
